title: The Kitchen Knife
text: Take a moment to look at the kitchen knife resting on your counter. You probably used it this morning to slice a piece of toast or cut an apple.
nxt: To your fingertips, that stainless steel edge feels razor sharp. You know that if you touch it carelessly, it can easily break your skin.

title: Science's Quiet Tools
text: Science, in its quiet quest to understand reality, has quietly built tools that make legendary weapons look like blunt stone clubs.

title: What Cutting Really Is
text: Have you ever wondered what actually happens when something is cut? At its fundamental level, cutting is not an act of destruction, but an act of separation.
nxt: When you press a blade down onto an object, physics dictates that pressure is simply force divided by surface area.

title: The Steel Limit
text: Traditional steel blades reach an inevitable physical limit.
nxt: Even the finest surgical scalpels made of hardened stainless steel can only be sharpened down to an edge roughly several hundred nanometers wide.

title: Nature's Glass
text: Nature, however, figured out a sharper solution long before humans invented metallurgy.
nxt: Deep inside volcanic regions, hot molten lava rich in silica cools so rapidly that mineral crystals have no time to form.
